sections.text:
Muhammad bin Abdullah, may God bless him and grant him peace, is the seal of the prophets and messengers. God sent him as a mercy to the worlds, to enlighten humanity after long ages of ignorance, darkness, and idolatry.

He was born an orphan in Mecca in the Year of the Elephant, and his mother died when he was young, so his grandfather Abdul Muttalib, who loved him dearly, took care of him, then his uncle Abu Talib, who defended him throughout his life.

Muhammad was known among his people in Mecca as “the honest and trustworthy” because of his honesty and honesty in trade. He never prostrated to an idol, did not drink alcohol, and stayed away from entertainment gatherings.

He used to isolate himself in the cave of Hira to contemplate the creation of the universe, away from the hustle and bustle of pre-Islamic times, searching for the truth.

At the age of forty, while he was in the cave, a revelation came down to him through the angel Gabriel, peace be upon him, and he hugged him and said to him: “Read.” The first verses of the Qur’an were: “Read in the name of your Lord who created.”

The Prophet began his call for monotheism secretly for three years, and his wife Khadija and his friend Abu Bakr believed in him, then God commanded him to speak out in the call.

When he declared his call publicly, he faced the most severe forms of torture and ridicule from the Quraish tribe, and they boycotted him and besieged him in Shaab Abi Talib for three years.

But he remained steadfast like a thorny mountain and did not give up his calling, until his wife Khadija and his uncle Abu Talib died in one year, which was called the Year of Sorrow.

God honored him with the event of the Night Journey, where he was taken on a journey from Mecca to Al-Aqsa Mosque, and taken up to the highest heavens, and there the five daily prayers were imposed as a gift to his nation.

He migrated to Medina (Yathrib) after the Quraysh’s harm intensified and they attempted to assassinate him in his bed, and there the Ansar received him with great warmth.

In Medina, he established the first Islamic state based on justice, equality, and fraternity between immigrants and Ansar, and established the Medina newspaper to regulate relations with the Jews.

The Prophet led many raids to defend Islam against the attacks of the Quraish and its allies. He was victorious at Badr, was tested at Uhud, and withstood the Battle of the Trench thanks to digging a trench around Medina.

The Prophet was a brilliant leader in the field, a merciful father who was kind to his children, and a just judge who did not differentiate between the honorable and the weak.

In the eighth year of the Hijra, the Prophet returned to Mecca as a conqueror with an army of ten thousand fighters, and entered it peacefully without bloodshed.

When the Quraish leaders who had expelled and tortured him stood before him, awaiting his verdict, he pardoned them and said his immortal word: “Go, for you are free.”

The Prophet performed the farewell Hajj and delivered a great sermon in which he established human rights and the sanctity of blood and treasure.

Through him, God completed the religion, completed the blessing, and revealed to him the Noble Qur’an, which God guaranteed to be preserved until the Day of Resurrection as an eternal miracle to be recited by Muslims in every place and time.

The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, died in the eleventh year of the Hijra in the lap of his wife Aisha, after establishing the foundations of Islam and leaving his nation on the white pilgrimage, day and night, leaving behind him a fragrant biography that illuminates the paths of the worlds.
